claim_being_audited: The Actor claims certification is compliant and evidentially supportable despite a known underperforming municipal permitting assistant segment, on the theory that aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and public guidance permits launch with documented limitations and post-deployment monitoring.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the named municipal permitting assistant gap was disclosed before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Launch documentation or model card showing the limitation was disclosed before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for the named-use-case gap.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Signed or otherwise admissible approval record granting risk acceptance for this specific gap before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: If disclosure did not occur, approved risk acceptance is the only policy-listed alternative basis in the record.

concern_ledger.concern: Materiality remains unresolved because the affected segment is named in two city pilot commitments and legal review is still pending.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final legal determination or other admissible evidence establishing non-materiality under the policy despite the named commitments.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy text says product labels like non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when named commitments or pending legal review exist.

concern_ledger.concern: The Actor overrelies on public model-card and monitoring guidance to justify certification.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible internal evidence satisfying the specific disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement, not general external governance guidance.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Those sources do not establish satisfaction of the internal policy requirement tied to a named launch use case.

decision_criteria: Use `compliant` only if admissible evidence shows the named-use-case gap either was disclosed as required or was covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Do not treat aggregate readiness, traffic share, or 'non-core' product labeling as sufficient to defeat materiality where the affected segment is named in customer commitments.
Treat pending legal review on disclosure as an unresolved compliance blocker unless other admissible evidence independently satisfies the policy requirement.
Public governance guidance may support good practice around documentation and monitoring, but it cannot substitute for satisfaction of the internal release policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide admissible evidence that the municipal permitting assistant limitation was disclosed in the model card or equivalent launch documentation before launch.
Provide an approved risk acceptance covering this specific named launch use case and evaluation gap, if disclosure was not made.
Provide the final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.

Provide admissible evidence showing the named city pilot commitments do not qualify as named launch use cases or contractual customer commitments under the policy, if that is the basis for certification.
specific_concerns: The named municipal permitting assistant segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two city pilot commitments, which makes materiality plausible under the policy text.
The release policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance for material limitations affecting named launch use cases before launch, and no admissible evidence shows either occurred.
Legal review is still open on whether the gap must be disclosed, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not independently resolve the disclosure obligation for a named affected use case.

The Actor's reliance on public model-card and monitoring guidance overclaims what those sources establish; they support documentation and monitoring practices, not waiver of an internal disclosure policy.
unsupported_claims: Certification is compliant on the present record.
Known limitations can be managed through documentation and monitoring without first resolving or satisfying the internal disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement for the named launch use case.
Public guidance provides sufficient support for certification without a material weakness disclosure decision.
